public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ThinLQ.sum_prefix_of_zero
public_declarations.exact_signature: theorem sum_prefix_of_zero {m n : ℕ} {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (hmn : m ≤ n) (f : Fin n → M) (hf : ∀ j, m ≤ j.val → f j = 0) : (∑ i : Fin m, f (Fin.castLE hmn i)) = ∑ j : Fin n, f j
inputs: Implicit naturals m,n and arbitrary carrier M.
An additive commutative monoid structure on M; no scalar multiplication, order, subtraction or cancellation is assumed.
A proof m≤n and an arbitrary Fin n-indexed family f.
The tail-zero condition applies to every j with m≤j.val, including the boundary j.val=m.
public_declarations.conclusion: The sum over the embedded length-m prefix equals the full length-n sum. It is not a converse characterizing vanishing tails.
proof: The prefix embedding is injective because equality of its values gives equality of the original Fin values.
Rewrite the prefix sum as the sum over the image of Fin m in Fin n.
Extend that image sum to all Fin n: a missing index cannot have value <m, because then it would have a prefix preimage.
Every omitted index therefore lies in the zero tail; adding it leaves the sum unchanged.
edge_cases: m=0: every f j must be zero, so the empty sum equals the full zero sum.
m=n: the tail hypothesis has no satisfying index and the embedding covers all indices.
n=0 forces m=0; both sums are empty.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ThinLQ.exists_factor_of_le
public_declarations.exact_signature: theorem exists_factor_of_le {m n : ℕ} (hmn : m ≤ n) (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ (R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ) (Q : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ), A = R * Q ∧ Q * Q.transpose = 1
inputs: Arbitrary implicit naturals m,n with m≤n.
An arbitrary m-by-n real matrix A.
No linear independence, nonzero rows, positivity, normalization, rank, numerical tolerance or oracle premise.
public_declarations.conclusion: There exist a square m-by-m real coefficient factor R and an m-by-n real row-orthonormal factor Q giving the exact equality A=RQ.
proof: Create n vectors f_i in ℝ^n: f_i is row i of A when i<m, and is the zero vector when i≥m.
Use dim(ℝ^n)=card(Fin n) to obtain b=gramSchmidtOrthonormalBasis hd f, a complete n-element orthonormal basis.

This provider normalizes each nonzero Gram-Schmidt residual in its original index slot and completes all zero-residual slots by a classical choice of additional orthonormal vectors. It does not require the input family to be independent.
For i,k<m set R_ik to the coordinate of f_i along b_k; equivalently R_ik=<b_k,f_i>. Set row k of Q to b_k.
For i<m and k≥m, i<k, so the provider's inverse-triangular coefficient theorem gives <b_k,f_i>=0.
The full basis expansion f_i=sum_{k<n}<b_k,f_i>b_k therefore truncates to its first m terms by sum_prefix_of_zero. Evaluating coordinate j gives A_ij=(RQ)_ij.
The selected first m vectors of an orthonormal basis remain orthonormal; their coordinate dot products are delta_kl, which proves QQ^T=I_m.

reasoning: simp for canonical Fin and real instances

edge_cases: m=0: R is 0-by-0 and Q is 0-by-n; both equations are vacuous in row indices.
n=0: m≤n forces m=0, so no positive number of unit vectors in zero-dimensional space is required.
A=0 with m>0: the proof chooses completion vectors; Q is still row-orthonormal. Its chosen coefficient R is zero. Returning Q=0 would violate the statement.
Zero initial rows or linearly dependent rows can produce zero residuals at arbitrary index positions; classical completion fills those positions.
m=n: the witness Q is square orthogonal, while A and R may remain singular.
Tall case m>n is outside this particular theorem's premise.
strength_boundary: The displayed witness actually also has R_ik=0 when i<k, by the same provider theorem applied within the prefix; this property is not included in the public existential conclusion.
The public theorem does not export the witness choice, a canonical basis, uniqueness, diagonal sign conditions, invertibility of R or a rank equality.
Orthonormality gives m independent rows of Q even when rank(A)<m. It does not claim the rows of Q form exactly the row space of A.

public_declarations.name: QuantumBlockEncoding.ThinLQ.exists_thin_lq
public_declarations.exact_signature: theorem exists_thin_lq {m n : ℕ} (A : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ) : ∃ (R : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin (min m n)) ℝ) (Q : Matrix (Fin (min m n)) (Fin n) ℝ), A = R * Q ∧ Q * Q.transpose = 1
inputs: An arbitrary m-by-n real matrix A.
public_declarations.conclusion: With k=min(m,n), there exist R of shape m-by-k and Q of shape k-by-n, exactly satisfying A=RQ and QQ^T=I_k. k is a dimension minimum, not rank(A).
proof: When m≤n, rewrite min(m,n)=m and invoke exists_factor_of_le.
When not m≤n, derive n≤m and rewrite min(m,n)=n.
In this tall branch choose R=A and Q=I_n; A*I_n=A and I_n*I_n^T=I_n by ordinary matrix identities.

reasoning: case split on natural dimension comparison

edge_cases: Strictly wide m<n: Q has exactly m orthonormal rows, including for rank-deficient A.
Square m=n: uses the m≤n branch, not the identity shortcut in the written proof.
Strictly tall m>n: Q=I_n and R=A; no row orthogonalization of A or lower-trapezoidal reduction is performed.
m=0,n>0: k=0 and both factors have empty row or intermediate indices.
n=0,m>0: k=0, R=A is m-by-0 and Q is 0-by-0; every required matrix-entry equation is vacuous in a column or row index.
m=n=0: the empty-wide branch applies; all matrices and equations are empty.
A=0 with k>0: Q must still have unit mutually perpendicular rows; k does not shrink to zero.
A of rank r<k: R can be singular or rank-deficient, and Q includes extra orthonormal directions. No promise rank(A)=k is made.

conventions.dimensions: m,n are arbitrary natural numbers, with zero allowed. Fin d indexes precisely 0,...,d-1. Fin.castLE hmn preserves numerical index and embeds a prefix.
conventions.matrix: Matrix (Fin m) (Fin n) ℝ is an m-row, n-column function-valued real matrix. Matrix multiplication contracts the shared finite index: (R*Q) i j = sum_k R i k * Q k j.
conventions.transpose: Q.transpose j k = Q k j; this is ordinary transpose, not a conjugate-transpose generalization. Scalars are specifically real.
conventions.identity: 1 is the identity matrix on the row index of Q, with entry delta_kl. For Fin 0 it is the unique empty square matrix, and the equations are vacuous.
conventions.orthonormal_rows: Q*Q.transpose=1 means sum_j Q k j*Q l j = if k=l then 1 else 0. Every actual row has norm 1 and distinct rows are perpendicular. For nonempty row index, Q cannot be the zero matrix.
conventions.ambient_euclidean: EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) is PiLp 2 of real coordinates, with the Euclidean inner product. WithLp.toLp 2 changes the normed wrapper, not the coordinates.
conventions.quantifier_boundary: There are no user-supplied typeclass hypotheses on either matrix theorem. Standard ℝ and Fin instances are inferred. The sum lemma alone is universe-polymorphic and assumes AddCommMonoid M.

original_reconstruction.completion_dependency: The wide case uses Mathlib's noncomputable indexed orthonormal-basis extension of nonzero normalized Gram-Schmidt residuals. Zero-residual slots receive orthogonal completion vectors, and the provider proves those vectors orthogonal to every original row. The inverse-triangular coordinate theorem therefore works even for rank-deficient matrices and non-prefix zero residual positions.

actual: Three exact symbolic existence/sum theorems over all stated dimensions.
Row, not column, orthonormality for Q.
No positivity or independence assumptions on A.
No approximation error or success-probability parameter.
Local wide witness construction via a completed orthonormal basis; trivial tall identity witness.
not_exported_or_certified: A public lower-triangular or lower-trapezoidal predicate on R.
A rank-minimal factorization with rank(A) rows.
A selected deterministic executable factorization procedure.
Numerically stable Gram-Schmidt, pivoting, rank revealing, finite-precision correctness, runtime, memory or operation counts.
Uniqueness or canonicality of factors; even square cases permit changes of orthonormal basis.
Column orthonormality Q^T Q=I_n for wide matrices. For k<n the latter would have rank n although Q has only k rows.
Quantum circuit, state preparation, block encoding, gates, ancilla cleanup, oracle access, postselection, phase convention, synthesis or amplification claims.
derived_but_not_named_public_claims: From A=RQ and QQ^T=I_k one can algebraically derive R=AQ^T. This is not an additional exported theorem in this module.
Q has full row rank and rank(R)=rank(A); these require further matrix/rank reasoning and are not stated here.
The particular wide proof witness is lower triangular by the provider coefficient theorem, but the existential statement forgets that property.
The rows of A lie in the span of rows of Q; equality of these row spaces would require full row rank of A and is not unconditional.

original_reconstruction.limits: This is a reconstruction of actual formal meaning, not a judgment of equivalence to withheld source mathematics. Triangularity of the particular wide witness is visible in its construction but is not a conjunct of either public matrix theorem. In the tall branch R=A and Q=I_n, so no general triangular factor is publicly or constructively supplied.
